prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web app composition study, 16:9 landscape
Primary request: Design a complete desktop solving screen for a murder deduction puzzle called ALIBI, direction: cinematic evidence reconstruction table. This must read as a real responsive application interface, not a poster, photograph, moodboard, game cover, or scene with text over it.
Structure: a narrow full-width case masthead; a slim left case-status rail; a dominant square illustrated house board occupying roughly 56% of the usable width in the center; a right suspect contact-sheet dossier; a compact command rail below the board; a strong accusation action anchored at the lower right.
Real content: MIDNIGHT DELIVERY; four suspects including a clearly marked victim; clues On the lamp and The only person on the shower; progress 0/4; timer; Place, Mark, Undo, Redo, Clear, Hint; Accuse.
Visual world: 1940s cinematic continuity board meets modern forensic reconstruction table. Matte near-black magnetic steel ground, cool graphite and smoky olive surfaces, projector amber as the main active color, oxblood red only for conflict/danger, bone-white evidence labels. Contact-sheet portraits, grease-pencil connector lines, magnetic number markers, perforated film-edge rhythm, subtle oblique projector light. The illustrated room board stays colorful, high-contrast, toy-like, and instantly legible with recognizable furniture; it is the brightest physical artifact.
Typography: condensed industrial sans headline, narrow technical labels, disciplined monospaced evidence text. Sharp corners, clipped tabs, no generic rounded cards, no pills, no glassmorphism, no neon cyberpunk, no cream parchment dashboard, no excessive decoration.
Composition option A — Reconstruction Stage: board is the unmistakable focal object centered like a lit film stage; evidence lines originate only from the selected suspect and terminate at exact board features; left rail is dense but narrow; right dossier is scannable; command controls remain familiar and accessible.
Show enough vertical depth to prove the whole solving screen, not just a hero. Use only semantic UI text; no invented claims, logos, testimonials, pricing, or watermark.
